interpretation: One on-only unchanged-workload diagnostic passes all thirteen original gates, stable installed/helper/observer inputs, complete sampling and zero remaining descendants. It does not qualify relative latency.

All 267 observed background compiles complete. Mean pool lease wall time is about 0.0026 ms in that thread and 0.0019 ms for named daemon-route requests. These observations do not support pool saturation as the failed serial HTTP-tail cause.

Mean background compile wall/thread CPU are about 6.108/0.619 ms. Native status is about 0.886/0.126 ms; directory pinning about 0.608/0.072 ms. Wrapped boundaries overlap and include instrumentation. Other includes foreground and maintenance work; no exact HTTP-sample correlation is claimed.
Each observed background response is 10,322 bytes. State validation averages about 0.010 ms CPU. Response size alone does not establish the HTTP cause or justify a protocol change.

A separate real empty-pipe component transfers 600 exact 448-byte frames, timing 500 unmodified calls before a distinct 100-call counting phase. It observes 100 selector constructions, readiness polls and closes, with about 0.0035 ms median wall/CPU per uninstrumented frame. This isolated small cost does not explain the failed HTTP boundary; product pipe transport is left unchanged.

Source inspection identifies one OS thread creation per native context-lane request despite the existing two-job bound. Lazy bounded native worker reuse is the next candidate to qualify, without attributing the failed HTTP comparison or claiming a benefit before matching-artifact checks.
No product runtime, native deadline, queue size, approval, SDK, priority or performance threshold changes follow from these diagnostics. Both original distribution HTTP failures remain retained.
